chapters.title: Opening moves
chapters.concept: The first roll of the game sets the tone. Some rolls make a valuable point right away: 3-1 makes your 5-point, 6-1 your bar point, 4-2 your 4-point. With the others you choose between splitting your back checkers and bringing builders down from the midpoint.

chapters.title: Early game
chapters.concept: After the first few moves, the book runs out and the board starts to matter. When GNU leaves a blot, hitting it is often right. When its checkers are safe, building your own position may matter more. Read the board before reaching for a standard move.

chapters.title: Making points
chapters.concept: Points in front of the opponent's back checkers are the backbone of a strong position. Your 5-point, 4-point and bar point block GNU's escape routes and give you a home board to attack with. Look for rolls that make a new point, and keep builders nearby for next time.

chapters.title: Hitting and attacking
chapters.concept: Hitting sends a checker back and costs your opponent pips and a tempo. It is strongest when your home board is solid, so a checker on the bar may struggle to come in. Hitting twice, or hitting while making a point, can win the game outright. Sometimes a quieter move is still better.

chapters.title: Safety or boldness
chapters.concept: Every blot you leave can be hit, and the number of rolls that hit it matters. Bold plays accept some risk to build a better position. Safe plays keep the shots down when getting hit would be costly. Weigh what you gain against what you lose if hit.

chapters.title: Primes and anchors
chapters.concept: A prime is a wall of consecutive points. Six in a row traps a checker completely, and even four or five make escaping hard. An anchor is a point you hold in the opponent's home board: a safe landing spot that keeps you in the game when you are behind.

chapters.title: Racing and bearing in
chapters.concept: Once the checkers have passed each other, the game is a pure race. Bring your checkers home without wasting pips, and think ahead: where they land in your home board decides how smoothly you bear off.

chapters.title: Bear-off
chapters.concept: With every checker home, the goal is to bear off as fast as possible. Take a checker off whenever you can, avoid gaps on your low points, and spread checkers so future rolls are not wasted.

chapters.title: Doubling
chapters.concept: The doubling cube is where many points are won and lost. Double when you are strong enough that a take or a pass both help you, but not so strong that playing on for a gammon is worth more. Double too early and you hand over the cube; too late and you lose your market.

chapters.title: Take or pass
chapters.concept: When doubled, compare playing on for twice the stake with giving up one point now. In a simple race you need about 25% winning chances to take, and owning the cube helps a little. Gammons against you raise the bar, so count them too.
